author: ribeye
dek: A Beavercreek fantasy manager benched Kenneth Walker III on Monday night, then watched him run for 173 yards and two touchdowns.
disclaimer: Parody: the Sanderson family of Beavercreek is fictional. The Chiefs' win over the Broncos is real, as reported by the Associated Press on Sep. 14, 2026.
headline: Beavercreek Man Benches Kenneth Walker, Watches Him Run for 173 Yards on Monday Night Football

ohio_quotes.quote: I benched Kenneth Walker because — and I quote myself — 'new team, Monday night, bad vibes.' He ran for 173 yards. I have never been so wrong about anything, including the time I said the Bengals would win the Super Bowl.
ohio_quotes.speaker: Greg Sanderson, Beavercreek

ohio_quotes.quote: He has now watched the 60-yard touchdown run eleven times. He counts the replays out loud. We are all very tired.
ohio_quotes.speaker: Karen Sanderson, Beavercreek

ohio_story: BEAVERCREEK, Ohio — Greg Sanderson had a plan for Monday night. The Beavercreek High School graduate, a veteran of the Beavercreek Basement League fantasy football league and a man who once drove to the Greene just to watch a Thursday night game on a bigger television, would start his usual running back, keep Kenneth Walker III on the bench, and enjoy a quiet evening. The plan lasted until the third quarter.

Walker, in his first game as a Kansas City Chief, took a fourth-and-1 carry 60 yards for a touchdown to open the second half, part of a 173-yard, two-touchdown night in the Chiefs' 31-10 rout of Denver. Greg watched it happen from his couch, a plate of Skyline coneys going cold on the coffee table, while his phone lit up with messages from the league group chat. "Every single person in the league texted me the same screenshot," Greg said. "My own brother texted me the screenshot. My brother does not even watch football. He watches the Dayton Dragons and leaves it at that."

The running back Greg started instead finished the night with 6.4 fantasy points, a total Greg described as "a number I will be hearing about until Christmas." He has already announced a new personal rule for the rest of the season — never bench a reigning Super Bowl MVP on a Monday night — and has printed it out and taped it to the fridge, next to the Beavercreek football schedule and a coupon for Marion's Piazza. Karen, for her part, has asked only that he stop narrating the 60-yard run in the style of a radio play-by-play announcer. "He does the crowd noise too," she said. "He does the crowd noise."
real_summary: The Kansas City Chiefs beat the Denver Broncos 31-10 on Monday Night Football on Sept. 14, 2026, in their season opener at Arrowhead Stadium. Patrick Mahomes, playing his first game back after surgery to repair ligaments in his left knee — hurt nine months earlier to the day against the Chargers — threw for 184 yards and two touchdowns and ran for a 15-yard score on the Chiefs' opening drive.

The night belonged to Kenneth Walker III, the reigning Super Bowl MVP, in his Chiefs debut after signing a three-year, $43.05 million deal in free agency. Walker carried 23 times for 173 yards and two touchdowns, including a 60-yard score on fourth-and-1 to open the third quarter — the most rushing yards by a Chiefs player since Jamaal Charles ran for 226 against Indianapolis in 2012.

Denver, which had ended Kansas City's nine-year run as AFC West champions, managed just 176 yards of offense. Bo Nix threw for 131 yards with an interception and a lost fumble, and offseason acquisition Jaylen Waddle had one catch for two yards. The win snapped a three-game Chiefs losing skid against Denver.
source_note: AP reporting, Sep. 14, 2026: Chiefs 31, Broncos 10; Mahomes' return from knee surgery; Walker's Chiefs debut.
